solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drag one's feet on stair carpet newly fitted

indicators.note: a carpet newly fitted has been laid afresh, so these letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dawdles over a staircase that has just had new carpet put down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly fitted' rearranges the thirteen letters of ON STAIR CARPET.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither and put off acting is what dragging one's feet means, an idiom for delay.

clue.text: Refuse to make a scathing comment

definitions.meaning: refuse as a noun means waste or garbage
as a verb, to criticise something harshly and dismiss it as worthless

explanation.definitionFit: Waste is one sense of the noun, and harsh dismissal is the verb sense, so both definitions are synonyms.

clue.text: Once set it may hold ice‑cream

indicators.note: set here means arranged differently, so the word once is rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that, once it has hardened, can be used to hold ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges ONCE; the surface makes it sound like jelly setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer cornet is the classic holder for a scoop of ice cream, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Appeal when vehicle overturns in amateur races

indicators.note: in places the turned vehicle within the races

parts.note: TT stands for the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: a vehicle that overturns is upside down, so the word for it is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle

explanation.surface: A plea made after a car flips over during an amateur motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy, a famous motorcycle race; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw or charm people is to appeal to them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: The storm created by Shakespeare

parts.note: a violent storm is the plain sense, and the play by Shakespeare whose title is that word is the other

explanation.surface: A dramatic storm brought about by the playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent windstorm is the word's meaning, and with 'The' it names Shakespeare's late play set on an island.

clue.text: Africa's best-known desert flower

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, a river, and the most famous one in Africa runs through the Sahara

explanation.surface: Asks for the most famous bloom that grows in Africa's deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as 'flow-er', a thing that flows; crosswords often use it for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa's longest river flows north through the Sudanese and Egyptian desert, so it is the famous desert waterway.

clue.text: There is a short girl here

indicators.note: short means contracted, as when there is becomes there's, losing a letter

parts.note: taken as the two words there and is

explanation.surface: Points out a little girl standing right here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' contracts THERE IS to THERE'S by dropping the I, then A follows; 'short' seems to describe the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so the clue's girl is a specific example.

clue.text: Fiddle just enough to satisfy examiner?

definitions.text: Fiddle just enough to satisfy examiner?

parts.words: Fiddle just enough to satisfy examiner?
parts.note: a violin is scraped with a bow, and scraping by an exam means passing it narrowly

explanation.surface: A violin student plays only well enough to pass the music examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' suggests cheating, but it is the instrument whose bowing is scraping.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass narrowly, only just reaching the required standard, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Narrowly failed, received school caning

definitions.meaning: lost by a tiny margin, as in a horse race
was punished with blows from the headteacher

explanation.walkthrough: In racing, losing by a horse's head is a close defeat; 'head' is also short for headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing idiom for a very close loss, and literally being beaten by the head teacher.

clue.text: Transport I catch for this meeting of governors

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a means of transport
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: Someone takes a taxi to get to a governors' meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior ministers who govern a country meet as a body under this name.

clue.text: French dramatist's second story about the Queen

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the story goes round the Queen

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A French playwright's next tale concerns the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay; MO for a second comes from 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventeenth-century French comic playwright of Tartuffe, so a named example of a French dramatist.

clue.text: Keen to bring singer back

indicators.note: bringing the singer back means reading her name in reverse

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to see a vocalist return.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and enthusiastic are both synonyms of keen in this sense.

clue.text: Fall off in spill

definitions.meaning: a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire

explanation.walkthrough: 'spill' is not an accident here but a lighting strip.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle gradually is the verb, and a slender candle or lighting strip is the noun.

clue.text: Labour staged walk-out?

definitions.meaning: Labour is the main party of the political ... in Britain
people who walk out have gone away

explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the UK's main left-of-centre party; walkers-out have departed the room.
explanation.definitionFit: The political wing that Labour belongs to, and the past tense of leave, meaning departed.

clue.text: Elect Russian leader

definitions.meaning: the surname of Russia's long-serving president

explanation.definitionFit: Voters install someone in office, a phrasal verb for electing, and it is also the Russian president's surname.

clue.text: Trace mislaid box

indicators.note: something mislaid is out of place, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to track down a box that has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaid' rearranges TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden packing case is a kind of box, so this is a synonym.

clue.text: Unwanted gas pipe?

definitions.meaning: the waste fumes from an engine
the tube on a car that carries away those fumes

explanation.definitionFit: Waste fumes vented by an engine, and the tailpipe that vents them from a car.

clue.text: About to be put back in school ground

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece within the word for school

parts.note: to school someone is to train them

indicators.note: put back means reversed, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is told to return to the school playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun but is the verb, to train; the reversed piece splits it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of land with its physical features is called ground or landscape.

clue.text: Fishy evidence that lady is married

parts.note: her is the pronoun for that lady
a wedding ring shows that someone is married

explanation.surface: Suspicious proof that a woman has wed.
explanation.walkthrough: A red herring is a misleading clue, so the definition is witty: evidence that smells of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading clue in a detective story is a red one of these, so it is evidence that is fishy.

clue.text: His depredations will affect stockholder

parts.note: stock here is livestock, and a thief who raids it harms the farmer who keeps it

explanation.surface: Sounds like a financial fraudster whose thefts hurt a shareholder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stockholder' suggests shares, but it means a farmer holding cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief steals livestock, so his raids hurt the farmer who owns the herd.

clue.text: Celebration drink for Pygmalion's love

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
tea is a common drink

explanation.surface: A party drink offered to Pygmalion's beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the sculptor Pygmalion fell for the statue he carved, brought to life and later named this.

clue.text: Artillery associated with assault

definitions.meaning: the legal offence of physical attack, paired with assault in law

explanation.definitionFit: A unit of guns is one sense, and unlawful physical attack, as in 'assault and', the other.

clue.text: Disapproval, we hear, increasing for drinking spree

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: boos are shouts of disapproval
up means rising or increasing

explanation.surface: Rising criticism of a night of heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is British slang for a heavy drinking party.
explanation.definitionFit: A party with heavy drinking is the British informal term for a drinking session.

clue.text: Able to come back after a stretch

definitions.text: Able to come back after a stretch

parts.words: Able to come back after a stretch
parts.note: a stretch suggests a prison term, but here it is stretching a material that springs back

explanation.surface: Sounds like a prisoner who can return after doing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch' is slang for a jail sentence, but it means pulling something taut.
explanation.definitionFit: Springy material returns to its shape once stretched, which is this adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Oats cooked in oven

indicators.note: cooked suggests the oats are prepared, but here it means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Porridge oats being baked in an oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges OATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln for drying hops is this kind of oven, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: A backward idiot, apart from all else

indicators.note: backward signals that the word for idiot is read in reverse

parts.note: a fool is an idiot

explanation.surface: A slow-witted person keeps away from everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like it describes the idiot but turns FOOL to LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant and detached, standing apart from others, is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Four-letter word that's used in place of another?

definitions.text: Four-letter word that's used in place of another?

parts.words: Four-letter word that's used in place of another?
parts.note: a four-letter word usually means a swear word, and this mild exclamation stands in for one; a punctuation stroke also replaces omitted letters

explanation.surface: Asks for a polite expression that substitutes for a rude one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four-letter word' implies an obscenity; the answer is a genteel substitute, and literally has four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild oath said instead of a curse, and the printed stroke that replaces a censored word's letters.

clue.text: This could be said from the platform

indicators.note: could be signals that the word said may become something else, a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Words that might be spoken by someone up on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges SAID; 'said' seems to be about speaking, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stage at the end of a hall for speakers is a kind of platform.

clue.text: It will remind me to go to doctor

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A note reminding the writer to see a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A short note serves as a reminder, so the definition describes its purpose.

clue.text: Flirt and irritate worker

parts.note: to gall someone is to irritate them
an ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone who makes advances and annoys a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashing, attentive man courting women is one sense, a ladies' man who flirts.

clue.text: Let care get arranged for female in tragedy

indicators.note: get arranged tells us to put these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to organise care for a woman in a tragic situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get arranged' rearranges LET CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The vengeful daughter of Agamemnon is the heroine of Greek tragedies by Sophocles and Euripides.

clue.text: Saucy proposal that may break deadlock

parts.note: fresh means cheeky or saucy
an approach is a proposal or overture

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that might end a stalemate.
explanation.definitionFit: A new way of tackling a problem is what can end a stalemate between parties.
